extracted.intended_audience: general public, policymakers, and researchers interested in U.S. foreign aid and MCC country eligibility
extracted.subtask_short: MCC country eligibility and selection criteria
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of the Millennium Challenge Corporation's principles, scorecard rules, and the 20 selection indicators used to determine country eligibility for compacts or threshold programs, plus related procedural requirements for application and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive selection (guiding principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before a country can become eligible to receive assistance, MCC's Board examines its performance on 20 policy indicators and selects compact-eligible countries based on policy performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes objective, indicator-based selection rather than discretionary political allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Country-led solutions (guiding principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCC requires selected countries to identify their priorities for achieving sustainable economic growth and poverty reduction; countries develop their MCC proposals in broad consultation within their society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Countries must lead design of proposals; MCC teams work in close partnership to help refine a program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Country-led implementation (guiding principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a country is awarded a compact, it sets up its own local Millennium Challenge Account (MCA) accountable entity to manage and oversee all aspects of implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation is country-run with rigorous, transparent monitoring (often via independent fiscal agents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Board selection factors
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board of Directors chooses countries based on three factors: policy performance as measured by the selection indicators on MCC's scorecard, the opportunity to reduce poverty in a country, and the availability of funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy performance is assessed via the 20 independent indicators; opportunity-to-reduce-poverty and funding constraints are considered alongside scorecard results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scorecard pass rules (how a country 'passes')
rubrics_metrics.description: A country is considered to 'pass' the scorecard if it: (i) passes at least 10 of the 20 indicators; (ii) passes the Control of Corruption indicator; and (iii) passes either the Civil Liberties or Political Rights indicator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three conditions are jointly required for compact eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring methodology: median-based vs static thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: For 16 of the 20 indicators, a country passes if its score exceeds the median score of its peer group; the remaining 4 indicators (Political Rights, Civil Liberties, Immunization Rates (if the median is above 90%, otherwise median-based), and Inflation) are scored based on a static threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer-group medians are by income-level peer groups; thresholds: Inflation must be under 15%; Immunization must be above 90% or the median (whichever is lower); Political Rights and Civil Liberties have fixed score cutoffs (see specific guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of third-party, transparent indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: All 20 indicators are compiled by third parties with no connection to MCC and are used to make grants without considering politics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MCC emphasizes reliance on publicly available, independent data sources (e.g., Freedom House, World Bank, WHO, UNESCO, IMF, Heritage Foundation, V-Dem, etc.) to ensure objective selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compact vs Threshold program distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: MCC signs either a compact or a threshold agreement: a compact is awarded if the country scores highly on the selection criteria indicators; a threshold program is a smaller grant used to assist a country close to meeting eligibility that shows a positive, upward trend on the selection criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Threshold programs are intended to help countries improve indicators so they can later become compact-eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application must specify a concrete project
rubrics_metrics.description: An eligible country must apply for a grant with a specific project in mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Country proposals should be concrete and country-led, describing prioritized interventions to achieve sustainable economic growth and poverty reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to create special purpose legal/implementation entity
rubrics_metrics.description: MCC requires that each partner government creates a special purpose legal entity that will be accountable for implementing the compact program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This entity (local MCA) manages and oversees implementation, enabling accountability and country-led execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and financial oversight requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitoring of funds is rigorous and transparent, often through independent fiscal agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Robust monitoring/oversight is expected as part of implementation to ensure accountability and reduce corruption or misuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil liberties (indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Civil liberties — Category: Ruling justly — Source: Freedom House.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored with a static threshold (page notes countries must score above 25 to pass). Used as one of the two political freedom indicators where passing either Civil Liberties or Political Rights is required to pass the scorecard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political rights (indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Political rights — Category: Ruling justly — Source: Freedom House.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored with a static threshold (page notes countries must score above 17 to pass). Passing Political Rights or Civil Liberties is required for the scorecard pass.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of Information (indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Freedom of Information — Category: Ruling justly — Sources: Reporters Without Borders, Centre for Law and Democracy, Access Now.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the 'Ruling justly' indicators; for most indicators passing is determined relative to peer-group median unless specified otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government effectiveness (indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Government effectiveness — Category: Ruling justly — Source: World Bank Institute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured by an independent data source and compared to peer medians for pass/fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule of law (indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule of law — Category: Ruling justly — Source: World Bank Institute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the 'Ruling justly' cluster and assessed via third-party data relative to peer medians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control of corruption (indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Control of corruption — Category: Ruling justly — Source: World Bank Institute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mandatory indicator: a country must pass Control of Corruption to pass the overall scorecard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immunization rate (indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Immunization rate — Category: Investing in people — Source: World Health Organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring is special: must have immunization coverage above 90% OR meet the median, whichever is lower (i.e., if median is above 90% the static 90% threshold applies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public expenditure on health (indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public expenditure on health — Category: Investing in people — Source: World Health Organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated using third-party data and compared to peer medians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Girls' primary education completion rate (indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Girls' primary education completion rate — Category: Investing in people — Source: UNESCO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicator measures completion rates for girls at primary level; passing typically by comparison to peer-group median.

rubrics_metrics.name: Girls' secondary education completion rate (indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Girls' secondary education completion rate — Category: Investing in people — Source: UNESCO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar role as primary completion rate; used to evaluate investment in people and gender/education outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public expenditure on education (indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public expenditure on education — Category: Investing in people — Sources: UNESCO and national sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses government investment in education; evaluated relative to peers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural resource protection (indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural resource protection — Category: Investing in people — Source: CIESIN/Yale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures policies and outcomes related to environmental/natural resource protections; compared to peer medians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Child Health (indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Child Health — Category: Investing in people — Source: CIESIN/Yale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses child health outcomes using third-party data and median comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inflation rate (indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inflation rate — Category: Economic freedom — Source: International Monetary Fund (WEO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored via a static threshold: a country's inflation rate must be under a fixed ceiling of 15 percent to pass (unless other methodological updates noted by MCC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade policy (indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trade policy — Category: Economic freedom — Source: The Heritage Foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses openness/quality of trade policy; compared to peer medians for pass/fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Land rights and access index (indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Land rights and access index — Category: Economic freedom — Sources: IFAD / V-Dem Institute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures security and accessibility of land rights; evaluated relative to peer medians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory quality (indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory quality — Category: Economic freedom — Source: World Bank Institute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses the ability of the government to formulate and implement sound policies and regulations; passed by median comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiscal policy (indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiscal policy — Category: Economic freedom — Source: IMF WEO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates macroeconomic fiscal health and policy; compared to peer medians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to Credit (indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to Credit — Category: Economic freedom — Sources: Findex, World Bank, IMF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures population/business access to financial services and credit; assessed versus peer medians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender in the Economy (indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gender in the Economy — Category: Economic freedom — Sources: Women, Business and the Law (World Bank, UCLA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates gender-specific legal and economic barriers; passing typically by median comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment Opportunity (indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employment Opportunity — Category: Economic freedom — Sources: V-Dem Institute, UCLA (newer indicator added to MCC scorecard).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses labor market opportunities and nondiscrimination; compared to peer medians for pass/fail.
